items.description: Reconcile the CR metadata Status lines so regenerate_catalog.py parses them
items.impact: advisory only: 14 CR docs whose '**Status**:' line the parser does not recognise (7 read 'Normative', EXT-06 reads 'Implemented', 6 have no Status line in the first 30 lines) are counted as 'open' in CATALOG.yaml's open_change_requests count (135). No gate fails; the count is informational.
items.proposed_action: DELIVERED 2026-10-21 (branch fix/cr-metadata-s21-conformance). Root cause was three distinct defects, not one: (1) MARKER STYLE: EXT-08..EXT-14 declared metadata as bare 'Status:' rather than the S21 '**Status**:' form; the gate reads only the bold form, so it reported present fields as missing. Repaired to the canonical convention shared by the other 152 CRs. (2) STATUS VOCABULARY: 10 CRs carried values outside {Proposed, Accepted, Rejected, Superseded, Draft} ('Implemented', 'Normative (...)', compound 'X; release withdrawn ...'). Normalised to the nearest approved token; the dropped annotation is already duplicated verbatim in each CR body, so no information was lost. (3) DEPENDENCY REFS: EXT-19..22 cited dependencies in the shorthand 'EXT-15' form, which no reference pattern resolves; expanded to the canonical 'CR-BP-94-EXT-15' form. Result: CR metadata gate CONFORMANT, rc=0, and CATALOG.yaml open_change_requests 135 -> 129. DELIBERATELY NOT DONE: CR-BP-03 and CR-BP-03C were left untouched. CR-BP-03's line is an unfilled template placeholder ('status: pending  # pending | accepted | rejected | re-landscaped') and CR-BP-03C declares no status at all. Assigning either an approved value would fabricate a governance decision nobody made; both are correctly counted as open, which is the honest reading of 'pending'.

items.description: Reconcile gate [9] CR Validation's registry classification with how CI invokes it
items.impact: scripts/conformance_result.py registers '[9] CR Validation (CR-META-001..006)' with the blocking flag False (advisory), while .github/workflows/ci.yml invokes the same gate with --strict, which promotes post-cutoff CRs to blocking. The registry's aggregate verdict has therefore never reflected this gate while CI has blocked on it for every PR since PR-13. Two independent surfaces disagree about the same gate's class.
items.proposed_action: Decide which surface is authoritative and make the other match. Either promote the registry entry to blocking (the gate is a real S21 enforcement gate and CI is right), or drop --strict from the CI step. IMP-011 made the gate satisfiable, so the first option is now viable; the second disables an enforcement gate and is not recommended.
